1	# Vocabulary
2	
3	Every document, identifier, and UI label uses these words exactly. If a better word appears, change it here first and then everywhere else (L2.21: understanding enables composition; shared words are the interface).
4	
5	## Propositions and links
6	
7	**Hypothesis.** The user's root input. A proposition asserted by `do()`, carrying the user's prior as a `user` belief. There is exactly one per graph.
8	
9	**Proposition.** A node. A *resolvable* claim — something that will be true or false by a date, judged by a named source. Never a vibe ("tensions ease"); always a check ("≥14 consecutive days of unrestricted commercial transit per Lloyd's List by 2026-11-01").
10	- `kind`: `hypothesis` · `event` · `market` (terminal; names an instrument) · `not_tradeable` (terminal; names the reason).
11	- `resolution`: `{criteria, source, by}` — all required (INV-1).
12	- `prior`: the model's marginal belief before parents are considered.
13	- `base_rate` (optional): `{reference_class, k, n, sources}`.
14	- `evidence[]`: `{claim, url, direction ∈ {+1, −1}, weight}`.
15	- `payoff` (market only): one of two shapes, told apart by a `kind` field. A **contract payoff** — `kind: contract` — names a venue, the venue's own identifier for the contract, its title, and the side you would take (`yes` or `no`). A **price payoff** — `kind: price` — names an instrument, a direction (`long` or `short`), and `move`, how far the price is expected to move if the claim comes out true, as a fraction (0.03 is three per cent). The rule behind both: the domain names *what you would trade*; what it costs — price, spread, and when we looked — is a market belief, fetched live.
16	
17	**Link.** An edge. A causal claim from one proposition to another.
18	- `mode`: `trigger` — horizontal/sequential causality (dominoes): fires once when the parent becomes true, effect persists and decays; removing the parent later does not undo it. `sustain` — vertical causality (the desk holds the apple): the effect exists only while the parent holds; removing the parent retracts the effect.
19	- `strength`: how much the link shifts the child's odds while active, on a log-odds scale (so several links add up instead of multiplying).
20	- `lag`: time from parent-true to link-active. `shape`: `impulse` (a one-time spike that fades with `half_life`) · `step` (switches on and holds) · `ramp` (builds up over `lag`).
21	- `rationale`: the mechanism in one to three sentences. `sources[]`. There is no field for how sure the model is about its own mechanism; `provenance` and the rationale carry that.
22	- `provenance`: see below. `reflexive`: market → world feedback; requires `lag > 0` (INV-6).
23	
24	**Provenance.** Where a number or link came from. `asserted` (model, no evidence) · `argued` (model, mechanism stated) · `documented` (cited sources) · `market_implied` (a live price) · `historical` (event study) · `user` · `simulated` (a probe). Encoded on every chip and wire (INV-2, INV-12).
25	
26	**Belief.** `{p, lo, hi, owner}` with `owner ∈ {model, user, market}` and `0 ≤ lo ≤ p ≤ hi ≤ 1` (INV-7). The three owners are stored and rendered separately and never averaged (INV-11). Rendered at two significant figures with the interval. `lo` and `hi` are the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself — how sure we are of the number, not how much the world can move.
27	
28	**Graph.** Propositions + links. A DAG after removing `reflexive` links; reflexive links unroll in time (INV-6). Has exactly one hypothesis and ≥1 terminal (INV-9). Immutable once created; changes are branches.
29	
30	## The multiverse
31	
32	**Intervention.** One operation on a graph:
33	- `do(n, value, at?)` — assert. Cuts the incoming links `n` has **at the moment the edit is applied**; a link inserted later is live. A timed assertion — `do(H, at=Oct 1)` says H holds from the 1st, not that H is sealed for ever. Ancestors unchanged (INV-3). This is what a hypothesis is.
34	- `observe(n, value)` — learn. Updates ancestors as well as descendants. Distinct verb in the UI.
35	- `insert(node, links[])` — "…but X happens." Adds a proposition and its links.
36	- `retune(link, strength)` — the user disagrees with a number.
37	- `refine(n → children[])` — split a proposition into finer sub-propositions; their combined likelihood must equal the original's (they *marginalize* back to `n`, INV-10). The brainstorm's "search deeper lines".
38	- `believe(n, belief)` — record the user's own belief on `n`. Lives in the branch so it replays and diffs; never alters `model` or `market` beliefs; not propagated in v1 (D8, INV-11). Propagating a user's world is a stretch (see `probes/`).
39	
40	**Branch.** A named, ordered list of interventions over a base graph. A branch *is* a patch. Branches compose by concatenation; `apply(g, [])` is `g` (INV-5). Branches may have a parent branch.
41	
42	**World.** A base graph with a branch applied and beliefs propagated. Replayable from `(base_id, branch, seed)` (INV-5, NFR-2). The base world is the empty branch.
43	
44	**Diff.** Between two worlds: per proposition, `unchanged` · `shifted` (with before → after) · `added` · `killed`; plus a ranked list of terminal deltas and a one-line natural-language summary. **`killed` means forced false, and nothing else** (decided 2026-09-17) — never "its number got small", and never "no path reaches it from the hypothesis any more", which is a fact about the *path* and is reported by the Inspector's path bar in those words. The ranking is the size of the move times the weakest provenance weight on the **best-backed route** from a differing edit's subject to that ending: over every such route, the one whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors; range width and agreement are columns beside it and are never multiplied in.
45	
46	**Version of the map.** One coherent set of numbers this model would have stood behind: every claim's likelihood drawn from its own stated range at once, never every low end together. The engine runs two thousand versions and eight worlds under each. The range on a computed number is the spread across versions; a change is read version by version, never by whether two ranges overlap.
47	
48	**Agreement.** The share of versions of the map in which a change moved the same way, each version counted by as much as it counted for the two numbers — so a version an observation left with no surviving world does not vote. Computed, never self-reported. A claim counts as `shifted` when it moved by .005 or more **and** agreement is at least 90%; agreement is then shown as its own column beside the change, never multiplied into the ranking. **On screen that column is headed *same direction*** (decided 2026-09-17), and the width column beside it is headed *how firm*; the field names stay `agreement` and `range_width`. Keeping the word *agreement* off this screen leaves it free for a run-to-run number — how far several independent generation runs agreed on a claim's likelihood — if one is ever earned. Stack 04 computes no such number: decision record 0015 ships the range the model stated and says *not yet* to an ensemble. If a second number ever exists: same idea, same rule, and wherever both could be meant, say which.
49	
50	**Locality.** An intervention changes only what is still connected to its subject in the graph the edit leaves behind (INV-4). Which claims those are depends on the operation, because the operations leave behind different graphs: `do` cuts the target's incoming arrows, so only the target and its descendants remain connected to it; `observe` cuts nothing, so its ancestors — and what those ancestors cause — are connected too. The per-operation **affected set** table in `multiverse/interventions.md` is the operational form, and the property test computes the set from the shape of the graph. The product's central correctness claim.
51	
52	## Sensitivity and drill-down
53	
54	**Sensitivity sweep.** One-at-a-time flip of every proposition; record Δ on each terminal.
55	
56	**Invalidation.** The proposition whose flip most damages a terminal *and* resolves before it *and* is publicly observable (INV-14). This is the stop-loss. **Take-profit** is the symmetric case. **Unhedgeable**: sensitive but not observable in time; listed, never used as a stop.
57	
58	**Tail.** A low-probability, high-magnitude proposition. Listed in its own strip with a suggested hedge; never averaged into an expected value.
59	
60	**Probe** (stretch). A modeling resource attached to one proposition: `monte_carlo` · `bayes_subnet` · `persona_redteam`. Output re-enters the graph as a `simulated` belief with its own rationale.
61	
62	**Value of information.** How much the trade depends on a proposition × how uncertain it is; ranks where a probe is worth its cost.
63	
64	## The finale
65	
66	**Thesis.** The compiled trade: `hypothesis`, `horizon`, `legs[]` (instrument, direction, size, driving proposition, model p, market p, edge), `entry`, `invalidation`, `take_profit`, `distribution` (p10/p50/p90, CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin)), `tails[]`, `caveats` (weakest links, unhedgeable, crowding).
67	
68	**Strategy export.** A declarative JSON rendering of a thesis with graph references justifying each leg; the shape a downstream trading agent could ingest.
69	
70	## Surfaces
71	
72	**Workbench.** The main screen: canvas + world-state strip + Inspector + tail strip + thesis dock.
73	**Tile.** A proposition's on-canvas card. **Port.** A typed input/output on a tile. **Wire.** A link's on-canvas rendering. **Inspector.** The persistent side panel; never a modal. **Delta rail.** The ranked terminal-delta list beside a diff; its two side columns are headed **how firm** (the width of the new number's range) and **same direction** (the share of versions of the map that moved the same way — the field called `agreement`; on screen the word *agreement* is kept free for a run-to-run number, if one is ever earned; decision record 0015 says not in stack 04). **Launchpad.** The empty state with the four seeded examples.
74	
75	## Interface words
76	
77	The six operations keep their code names in code, in the wire format and in this document — `do`, `observe`, `insert`, `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — and none of those words appears on screen. These are the words the user reads. Change a button here first, then everywhere else.
78	
79	| Code name | The button | The badge afterwards | What the interface says it means |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** | "Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it" |
82	| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date**, and **Did not happen · date** where the news is that it did not (Kent, 2026-09-21, G12) | "This is news — update what came before it too" |
83	| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** | A claim and its arrows arrive together |
84	| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** | "You moved this arrow from +0.7 to +0.3" |
85	| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** | The finer claims add back up to the one they replace |
86	| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge | Your number sits beside the model's and the market's |
87	| none | **Build the map** | none — the map is the answer | "Turn what I typed into a map of what it would cause" |
88	| none | **Change this claim** (and **Change this push**, on an arrow) | none — it opens the buttons above, and they earn the badges | "Show me what I can do to this" |
89	
90	**One of these rows has no control on screen in this build.** **Split this claim** is not implemented, and an operation that does nothing is not offered — a control that takes a press and then explains that it cannot act is still a control a reader counted and cannot use. Its words are settled here for the day it arrives.
91	
92	**Suppose this is false** is implemented and is offered, beside **Suppose this is true**; the two share one row because they are one operation with one badge. The panel carries, under each of the two easiest to confuse, that operation's own line from the last column of this table, so the difference is read before the press rather than after it.
93	
94	**Change this claim** is the second of that table's two labels with no code name behind it, because it opens the operations rather than being one. It is the way in for somebody working the screen with a mouse, and it sits in the head of the panel that says why a number is what it is: on a claim it reads **Change this claim**, on an arrow **Change this push** — the same words as the button inside that changes the arrow's number, because it is the same thing asked for, and the two are never on screen at once. It is drawn only while the operations are shut, since a way in that is already in is not a control. The keyboard's way in is `E` and the command palette's is a command of the same name; where a screen has to name the way in rather than draw it — the change list with nothing on it yet — it uses these words too.
95	
96	One more badge is **derived**: no button produces it. **Retracted · date · by "…"** appears on a claim that was supposed true and has since been pushed back down by a later edit — what was holding this up was removed. It names the edit responsible and the day it landed (UX-14; the mechanism is in `multiverse/interventions.md`).
97	
98	**Build the map** is the one button in that table with no code name behind it, because it starts a generation rather than editing a map: there is no intervention called *build*. It is the only button on the input bar, and it is the same button on both doors — Explore and Verify differ by whether the destination field has anything in it, and a button whose label changed as you typed would be a control moving under you. Not *Generate*, which is the pipeline's word rather than the reader's.
99	
100	### Words the growing map uses
101	
102	Four things a reader sees only while a map is being generated. What each is, and what it is never allowed to become, is in `workbench/streaming-growth.md`.
103	
104	**Skeleton tile.** A reserved rectangle standing where a claim is about to arrive: the tile's own box, one line of words, and nothing else. Never a number, never an identifier on the map, and never a shimmer — it is a space held open, not a thing pretending to load.
105	
106	**Refusal strip.** The list beside a growing map of every proposal the map's own rules turned down: one row each, carrying what the model wrote and the validator's own sentence for each rule it broke. Nothing is trimmed, merged or summarised away.
107	
108	**Receipt strip.** The lines beneath it saying what the run cost — the model, the calls, the tokens in and out, the tokens read from cache, the web searches, the dollars, how long it took, and whether it ran live or from a recording. Every one of them is a number the engine sent; the screen adds nothing up.
109	
110	**Replay badge.** The mark on the canvas saying this session is playing a recording rather than calling a model, with the day the recording was made. It is a fact about the session, not a badge on a claim, and no button produces it.
111	
112	## Words for a number that is not there
113	
114	An empty slot never shows a blank, a zero or a placeholder: it shows words and, one hover or one click away, a reason. These are the words; change them here first. There are **five** kinds of absence, and the last two — a number the engine refused to work out, and an ask that did not come back — are kinds of their own rather than shades of *no engine yet*.
115	
116	| Where | On the tile | The reason, read in the Inspector and on the chip's hover |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| No market price, on a `market` claim | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff." |
119	| No market price, on an `event` or the `hypothesis` | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim." |
120	| No market price, on a `not_tradeable` ending | **no market**, with the claim's own stored reason **on the tile** — that reason is a finding, not boilerplate | the same stored reason |
121	| No number of your own yet | **—** and *add yours* | "You have not given a number for this claim." |
122	| Nothing has been computed | **no engine yet** | "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet." |
123	| The engine **refused** to work it out | **not worked out** | the refusal's own reason, naming what was refused — for a branch that does not fit the map: "The engine would not work this map out from this branch: the branch does not fit the map. Every reason is beside the map, and nothing on the map has changed." |
124	| The **ask did not come back** | **the ask did not come back** | the failure's own sentence, and what to do about it: "… Select this arrow again to ask once more." |
125	
126	**Why the last three are three rows and not one.** *No engine yet* says nothing has run and invites waiting. *Not worked out* says the engine was asked, answered, and would not — which invites repairing the thing it turned down, and which will say the same thing every time until somebody does. *The ask did not come back* says the engine is there, it was asked, and one attempt got no reply — which invites asking again, and which may well be gone by the time you do. Three different facts about the same empty slot, and a reader who cannot tell them apart will wait for an answer that is never coming, or repair something that was never broken.
127	
128	The code carries the difference as three kinds — `no_engine`, `refused` and `ask_failed`, beside `no_market` and `not_said` — rather than as a difference in the words, because words are not something code can read back. **The last one is the only absence that is never kept**: it is not a fact about the map, so nothing files it with the answers.
129	
130	## Words we do not use
131	
132	*Prediction* (we model arguments, not oracles) · *scenario* (ambiguous between branch and world) · *edge* when we mean a link (reserve *edge* for model-vs-market spread) · *node* in UI copy (say tile or proposition) · *confidence*, at all — there is no confidence field on anything. A link's standing is its `provenance` (a receipt we write), its rationale, and the range on the belief; a number for how much things computed independently agreed is called *agreement* — defined under *The multiverse* above — and is computed, never self-reported.

**Sensitivity sweep.** One-at-a-time flip of every proposition; record Δ on each terminal.

**Invalidation.** The proposition whose flip most damages a terminal *and* resolves before it *and* is publicly observable (INV-14). This is the stop-loss. **Take-profit** is the symmetric case. **Unhedgeable**: sensitive but not observable in time; listed, never used as a stop.

**Tail.** A low-probability, high-magnitude proposition. Listed in its own strip with a suggested hedge; never averaged into an expected value.

**Probe** (stretch). A modeling resource attached to one proposition: `monte_carlo` · `bayes_subnet` · `persona_redteam`. Output re-enters the graph as a `simulated` belief with its own rationale.

**Value of information.** How much the trade depends on a proposition × how uncertain it is; ranks where a probe is worth its cost.

## The finale

**Thesis.** The compiled trade: `hypothesis`, `horizon`, `legs[]` (instrument, direction, size, driving proposition, model p, market p, edge), `entry`, `invalidation`, `take_profit`, `distribution` (p10/p50/p90, CVaR₅, max drawdown, P(ruin)), `tails[]`, `caveats` (weakest links, unhedgeable, crowding).

**Strategy export.** A declarative JSON rendering of a thesis with graph references justifying each leg; the shape a downstream trading agent could ingest.

## Surfaces

**Workbench.** The main screen: canvas + world-state strip + Inspector + tail strip + thesis dock.
**Tile.** A proposition's on-canvas card. **Port.** A typed input/output on a tile. **Wire.** A link's on-canvas rendering. **Inspector.** The persistent side panel; never a modal. **Delta rail.** The ranked terminal-delta list beside a diff; its two side columns are headed **how firm** (the width of the new number's range) and **same direction** (the share of versions of the map that moved the same way — the field called `agreement`; on screen the word *agreement* is kept free for a run-to-run number, if one is ever earned; decision record 0015 says not in stack 04). **Launchpad.** The empty state with the four seeded examples.

## Interface words

The six operations keep their code names in code, in the wire format and in this document — `do`, `observe`, `insert`, `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — and none of those words appears on screen. These are the words the user reads. Change a button here first, then everywhere else.

| Code name | The button | The badge afterwards | What the interface says it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** | "Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it" |
| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date**, and **Did not happen · date** where the news is that it did not (Kent, 2026-09-21, G12) | "This is news — update what came before it too" |
| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** | A claim and its arrows arrive together |
| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** | "You moved this arrow from +0.7 to +0.3" |
| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** | The finer claims add back up to the one they replace |
| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge | Your number sits beside the model's and the market's |
| none | **Build the map** | none — the map is the answer | "Turn what I typed into a map of what it would cause" |
| none | **Change this claim** (and **Change this push**, on an arrow) | none — it opens the buttons above, and they earn the badges | "Show me what I can do to this" |

**One of these rows has no control on screen in this build.** **Split this claim** is not implemented, and an operation that does nothing is not offered — a control that takes a press and then explains that it cannot act is still a control a reader counted and cannot use. Its words are settled here for the day it arrives.

**Suppose this is false** is implemented and is offered, beside **Suppose this is true**; the two share one row because they are one operation with one badge. The panel carries, under each of the two easiest to confuse, that operation's own line from the last column of this table, so the difference is read before the press rather than after it.

**Change this claim** is the second of that table's two labels with no code name behind it, because it opens the operations rather than being one. It is the way in for somebody working the screen with a mouse, and it sits in the head of the panel that says why a number is what it is: on a claim it reads **Change this claim**, on an arrow **Change this push** — the same words as the button inside that changes the arrow's number, because it is the same thing asked for, and the two are never on screen at once. It is drawn only while the operations are shut, since a way in that is already in is not a control. The keyboard's way in is `E` and the command palette's is a command of the same name; where a screen has to name the way in rather than draw it — the change list with nothing on it yet — it uses these words too.

One more badge is **derived**: no button produces it. **Retracted · date · by "…"** appears on a claim that was supposed true and has since been pushed back down by a later edit — what was holding this up was removed. It names the edit responsible and the day it landed (UX-14; the mechanism is in `multiverse/interventions.md`).

**Build the map** is the one button in that table with no code name behind it, because it starts a generation rather than editing a map: there is no intervention called *build*. It is the only button on the input bar, and it is the same button on both doors — Explore and Verify differ by whether the destination field has anything in it, and a button whose label changed as you typed would be a control moving under you. Not *Generate*, which is the pipeline's word rather than the reader's.

### Words the growing map uses

Four things a reader sees only while a map is being generated. What each is, and what it is never allowed to become, is in `workbench/streaming-growth.md`.

**Skeleton tile.** A reserved rectangle standing where a claim is about to arrive: the tile's own box, one line of words, and nothing else. Never a number, never an identifier on the map, and never a shimmer — it is a space held open, not a thing pretending to load.

**Refusal strip.** The list beside a growing map of every proposal the map's own rules turned down: one row each, carrying what the model wrote and the validator's own sentence for each rule it broke. Nothing is trimmed, merged or summarised away.

**Receipt strip.** The lines beneath it saying what the run cost — the model, the calls, the tokens in and out, the tokens read from cache, the web searches, the dollars, how long it took, and whether it ran live or from a recording. Every one of them is a number the engine sent; the screen adds nothing up.

**Replay badge.** The mark on the canvas saying this session is playing a recording rather than calling a model, with the day the recording was made. It is a fact about the session, not a badge on a claim, and no button produces it.

## Words for a number that is not there

An empty slot never shows a blank, a zero or a placeholder: it shows words and, one hover or one click away, a reason. These are the words; change them here first. There are **five** kinds of absence, and the last two — a number the engine refused to work out, and an ask that did not come back — are kinds of their own rather than shades of *no engine yet*.

| Where | On the tile | The reason, read in the Inspector and on the chip's hover |
|---|---|---|
| No market price, on a `market` claim | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim; what you would trade is on the payoff." |
| No market price, on an `event` or the `hypothesis` | **no market** | "No venue quotes this claim." |
| No market price, on a `not_tradeable` ending | **no market**, with the claim's own stored reason **on the tile** — that reason is a finding, not boilerplate | the same stored reason |
| No number of your own yet | **—** and *add yours* | "You have not given a number for this claim." |
| Nothing has been computed | **no engine yet** | "Nothing has worked this number through the map yet." |
| The engine **refused** to work it out | **not worked out** | the refusal's own reason, naming what was refused — for a branch that does not fit the map: "The engine would not work this map out from this branch: the branch does not fit the map. Every reason is beside the map, and nothing on the map has changed." |
| The **ask did not come back** | **the ask did not come back** | the failure's own sentence, and what to do about it: "… Select this arrow again to ask once more." |

**Why the last three are three rows and not one.** *No engine yet* says nothing has run and invites waiting. *Not worked out* says the engine was asked, answered, and would not — which invites repairing the thing it turned down, and which will say the same thing every time until somebody does. *The ask did not come back* says the engine is there, it was asked, and one attempt got no reply — which invites asking again, and which may well be gone by the time you do. Three different facts about the same empty slot, and a reader who cannot tell them apart will wait for an answer that is never coming, or repair something that was never broken.

The code carries the difference as three kinds — `no_engine`, `refused` and `ask_failed`, beside `no_market` and `not_said` — rather than as a difference in the words, because words are not something code can read back. **The last one is the only absence that is never kept**: it is not a fact about the map, so nothing files it with the answers.

## Words we do not use

*Prediction* (we model arguments, not oracles) · *scenario* (ambiguous between branch and world) · *edge* when we mean a link (reserve *edge* for model-vs-market spread) · *node* in UI copy (say tile or proposition) · *confidence*, at all — there is no confidence field on anything. A link's standing is its `provenance` (a receipt we write), its rationale, and the range on the belief; a number for how much things computed independently agreed is called *agreement* — defined under *The multiverse* above — and is computed, never self-reported.

content.content:
1	# The Inspector — why is this number what it is
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	Every number on this canvas has to be able to say where it came from. The Inspector is where it says
6	it.
7	
8	Select a claim and the panel gives you the whole of it: the full wording, how it will be judged and
9	by whom, the outside view it started from, all three beliefs with their owners kept apart, the
10	evidence, and — once the engine runs — the decomposition that turns the number into an argument you
11	can disagree with line by line. Select an arrow and it gives you the mechanism in a sentence, how
12	hard it pushes read back in words, what kind of push it is, how long it takes, what it does over
13	time, its sources with the day each was fetched, and where it came from.
14	
15	It is **one persistent side panel, and there are no pop-ups anywhere in this product** (UX-10). A
16	dialog you must dismiss is a veto condition; so is a number whose origin cannot be named in one
17	click (NFR-1). Where a value does not exist the panel says so **in words, with a reason** — never a
18	blank, never a zero, never a stand-in. In this stack that reason is usually *"no engine yet"*, which
19	is an honest sentence rather than a hole.
20	
21	**Every engine-computed figure quoted below is read from one generated file.** [`docs/worked-numbers.txt`](../../docs/worked-numbers.txt) is written by `make numbers` from the shipped engine on the Strait of Hormuz map, at that example's own seed and the shipped loop sizes, and the build fails when it goes stale. Every line in it starts with a name a passage can cite — `B · base · reading` — and the numbers a person typed into the example are kept in a part of their own, apart from the numbers the engine worked out. A figure is quoted here only where it teaches something; the file is where it is kept true, so the day the arithmetic changes, the diff of that one file is the whole list of what moved.
22	
23	[`keyboard-and-access.md`](keyboard-and-access.md) covers reaching and reading the panel without a
24	mouse, and owns the rendering rule behind INV-7 — two significant figures, and the range never
25	omitted.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Data model
30	
31	`ClaimDetail` and `LinkDetail` are **projections of `ClaimView` and `LinkView`**, the per-claim and
32	per-arrow records on `WorldView`, all defined in [`diff-view.md`](diff-view.md). `BeliefView` — one
33	likelihood with its range and a name on it — is defined in
34	[`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md). This panel takes the fields it draws and adds
35	nothing of its own:
36	
37	```ts
38	interface InspectorProps {
39	  /** What is selected. Nothing selected is a real state with its own copy, not a blank panel.
40	      The third kind is the generation itself — not a claim and not an arrow, but the run that
41	      produced them; see B7. */
42	  subject:
43	    | { kind: "claim"; id: string }
44	    | { kind: "link"; id: string }
45	    | { kind: "generation"; id: string }
46	    | null;
47	  world: WorldView;          // frontend/src/world/types.ts
48	  onSelect: (subject: InspectorProps["subject"]) => void;
49	}
50	
51	/** The claim half, drawn top to bottom in this order. */
52	interface ClaimDetail {
53	  claim: string;                       // the full wording, never ellipsized here
54	  kind: "hypothesis" | "event" | "market" | "not_tradeable";
55	  resolution: { criteria: string; source: string; by: string };   // all three required (INV-1)
56	  prior: BeliefView;
57	  baseRate: Known<{ referenceClass: string; k: number; n: number; sources: SourceView[] }>;
58	  beliefs: { model: Known<BeliefView>; user: Known<BeliefView>; market: Known<BeliefView> };
59	  evidence: readonly EvidenceView[];   // claim, address, direction, weight
60	  // No `decomposition` field: there is none on the world and none on the wire. The block is
61	  // assembled from fields that are each read — `prior` here, `strength`/`mode`/`lag`/`provenance`
62	  // and the fetched `conditional` on each incoming arrow, `beliefs.model` as the result — and not
63	  // one line of it is arithmetic. See B2.
64	  rangeShares?: Record<string, number>;// the reserved band slot; stack 06, nothing reads it here
65	  pathProduct: Known<PathProduct>;     // INV-8; arrives on the world, never multiplied here
66	}
67	```
68	
69	`LinkDetail` is `LinkView` with nothing added and nothing left out: the panel draws `rationale`,
70	`strength`, `mode`, `lag`, `shape`, `halfLife`, `sources` and `provenance`, in that order — B4 shows
71	the result. `Known<T>` and `Absence` — a value, or a kind of absence with the sentence that goes
72	beside it — are defined once in [`diff-view.md`](diff-view.md); every optional value here is one, so
73	no code path can render an absence as anything but its reason.
74	
75	**A push**, which the panel shows for every arrow, is a link's `strength`: a signed amount added on
76	the **log-odds scale** — the scale on which separate influences add up instead of multiplying. A
77	positive push moves the claim at the arrow's head toward coming true; a negative one moves it away.
78	
79	**Tokens read:** `--surface-raised` (the panel), `--hairline` (its one edge and its rules), `--text`
80	and `--text-muted`, `--font-mono` for every number, `--space-1` … `--space-4`, the likelihood ramp
81	`--p-0` … `--p-4`, `--accent`, `--focus` — all defined in
82	[`color-motion-type.md`](color-motion-type.md), where a direction is also rendered only through
83	`DirectionReadout`, which owns those tokens. This chapter defines none.
84	
85	**Shared components:** `OriginMark` (the three-step provenance mark) and the belief chip. Each is
86	**one component**, drawn by the wire and the tile as well, so the mark on a wire and the word in
87	this panel cannot drift apart.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Behaviour
92	
93	Worked on the Hormuz map (the cast is in [`README.md`](README.md)). This chapter uses **B** *Brent
94	crude settles below $68 for five sessions* — the busiest claim on the map, three arrows in (**H**,
95	**C**, **R**) and three out (**M1**, **M2**, and back to R) — and the arrow **H → B**.
96	
97	### B1 — A claim, top to bottom
98	
99	Select B's tile. The panel fills, in this order, and nothing opens over the canvas:
100	
101	```
102	Brent crude settles below $68 for five sessions.                       event
103	
104	RESOLVES
105	  Front-month Brent crude futures settle below $68.00 on five
106	  sessions, consecutive or not, within the window.
107	  judged by   ICE Brent front-month settlement prices
108	  by          2026-10-15
109	
110	BASE RATE
111	  —  no reference class recorded for this claim
112	
113	PRIOR
114	  .28 (.15–.42)          model
115	
116	BELIEFS
117	  model    .28 (.15–.42)
118	  stated range · not computed
119	  This range is stated, not computed — it says how sure the elicitation
120	  was. Nothing has worked this number through the map yet.
121	  user     —
122	  market   no market · no venue quotes this claim
123	
124	EVIDENCE
125	  —  no clippings attached to this claim
126	
127	WHY THIS NUMBER
128	  —  no engine yet
129	```
130	
131	Five things to read off that:
132	
133	* **The resolution triple is never optional.** Criteria, the source that adjudicates, and the date —
134	  all three, on every claim (INV-1, *checkable*: a claim nobody can score is not a claim).
135	* **Which sentence sits under the model row is decided by one field.** `WorldView.versions` — how
136	  many versions of the map the engine ran — is present only when something was computed. **Absent**,
137	  as here and everywhere in this stack, the row reads the **stated** pair above and **the reserved
138	  band slot is not drawn at all**: there is no computed band for it to explain. **Present**, the row
139	  reads record 0014's *model interval, uncalibrated · how sure we are of `.40` — not how much the
140	  world can move*, and the slot appears beneath it. The two sentences are written once and shared
141	  with the belief chip ([`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md)) so they cannot drift.
142	* **The model row here is the prior's own numbers, and that is not a coincidence.** Every
143	  `beliefs.model` in the fixture equals its `prior`, because nothing has been computed into it — so
144	  the stated sentence describes exactly what the row holds. Run the engine over this map and B comes
145	  out `.40 (.24–.56)`, which is the number the computed sentence above would be about.
146	* **Four things are genuinely absent on B, and each absence says which kind it is.** The **tile**
147	  shows `no market` and nothing else; **this panel is where the reason is read** — chosen by the
148	  claim's `kind` and written once in [`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md). B is an `event`, so it
149	  reads *"no venue quotes this claim"*; a `market` claim adds *"; what you would trade is on the
150	  payoff"*; a `not_tradeable` ending has its own stored reason, which is a finding and stays on its
151	  tile too. The **user** slot is the one absence drawn as a bare dash: an invitation to type your own
152	  number, where a sentence would read as an error rather than an offer.

162	### B2 — The decomposition: a number that can say why
163	
164	Under **WHY THIS NUMBER** the panel lays out the argument for the claim's number. The layout is the
165	one [`../graph/belief.md`](../graph/belief.md) §B4 draws — prior, one line per incoming arrow with
166	its push and its reason, then the result — and this panel copies it rather than inventing a second.
167	§B4's numbers are its own illustration and are not B's: B's prior is `.28 (.15–.42)`, it has no base
168	rate, and it has three incoming arrows, not two.
169	
170	**There is no `decomposition` field, and the block is not one thing the world hands over**
171	*(corrected 2026-09-20, stack 04a, on building it)*. This chapter said the world carried the block
172	whole and the panel rendered it or rendered nothing. It does not: the engine's world has no such
173	field, and the wire has none. What the panel does instead is put together lines it each reads —
174	`prior` from the claim, the push and its reason from each incoming arrow, the arrow's conditional
175	where one has been fetched, and `beliefs.model` as the result — and the rule the old wording was
176	protecting survives untouched, because not one of those lines is arithmetic done here.
177	
178	Four rules about it:
179	
180	1. **One line per incoming arrow the world carries** — not a selection. B's real block has three,
181	   the third being R → B at −1.2.
182	2. **Feedback arrows are not lines of the block.** A market acting back on the world it measures is
183	   set aside before the engine works the map through ([`../multiverse/interventions.md`](../multiverse/interventions.md)),
184	   so it contributed nothing to the number at the foot, and listing it among the pushes would hand
185	   the reader a cause the engine never gave. It is listed below them under the outline's own words,
186	   **fed back into by**, with a sentence saying it has not pushed on this number and why. A claim
187	   whose only incoming arrow is a feedback one says nothing points at it — which is what the engine
188	   did. *(Added 2026-09-20, stack 04a, on building it.)*
189	3. **No line may be a number whose owner cannot be named** — `belief.md`'s rule, inherited here.
190	4. **This panel never computes the block.** A canvas that added up its own pushes would be a second
191	   engine, and two engines disagree. Each line is a field read and printed; the line at the foot
192	   says on screen that nothing here was added up.
193	
194	**No line of it is ever merely missing** *(decided 2026-09-17 as "the whole block, or none of it";
195	restated 2026-09-20 to match what was built)*. The question was whether the panel might draw an
196	arrow's pushes while leaving out the result line. The answer is that every line is always drawn and
197	a line with no number says its absence and why, which is the rule the whole panel runs on — so the
198	result line reads *"no engine yet"*, with its reason, rather than being left off. A block missing
199	its last line reads as a sum somebody forgot to finish, and the reader cannot tell that from a sum
200	that went wrong; a last line that says why it is empty cannot be mistaken for either.
201	
202	**A claim that moved only because some versions started counting more says so, here.** Observing one
203	claim reweights the versions of the map — a version under which the observation was likely counts
204	for more than one under which it was a fluke (record 0014 §F) — and a claim with **no causes** can
205	move by that reweighting alone, because inside every single version its answer is its own prior in
206	both worlds and the paired difference is exactly zero. On Hormuz, observing **C** moves **H**, which
207	nothing on the map causes. Without a word about it the reader opens H and finds a number that moved,
208	a prior, and nothing in between to explain it.
209	
210	So the panel prints one sentence, word for word:
211	
212	> this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more.
213	
214	**Where it sits:** under **WHY THIS NUMBER**, as the first line of that section, above the
215	decomposition — because it is a fact about the reading of the number, and the decomposition is the
216	reading (the same shape as which sentence sits under the model row, Kent's K4).
217	
218	**When it shows:** only when the panel is open on a claim in a world being compared against another,
219	and the engine's own diff row for that claim carries the field saying so — a field the engine writes
220	in `domain/diff.py` and 04a's bottom pull request generates into `frontend/src/api/schema.ts`
221	([`../multiverse/diff.md`](../multiverse/diff.md) names it). Never otherwise, and **never worked out
222	here**: the browser does not compare a same-direction share against zero, does not check whether a
223	claim has incoming arrows, and does not infer this from a decomposition with no lines in it. It reads
224	the field or it says nothing.

256	Select the wire from H to B. Same panel, different subject; still no pop-up:
257	
258	```
259	The Strait of Hormuz reopens…   →   Brent crude settles below $68…
260	
261	WHY
262	  The war-risk premium priced into crude unwinds once transit data confirms
263	  the lane is open. It is a one-time repricing, not a standing discount.
264	
265	PUSH      +1.6 — a strong push toward
266	KIND      trigger — a domino: it fires once when the strait opens, and the
267	          effect stays put and fades on its own. Standing the first domino
268	          back up does not stand this one back up
269	DELAY     2 days from the strait opening

278	     for this arrow

281	* **The push is read back in words as well as a number.** `+1.6 — a strong push toward` is data
282	  already on the link and needs no arithmetic, which is why the wire's midpoint chip can show it
283	  before the engine exists. The words come from the **five bands** in
284	  [`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md) — [`../graph/link.md`](../graph/link.md)'s four
285	  anchors with the gaps filled and one band below 0.25 (Kent, 2026-09-17) — and this panel uses

287	  against*. The chip writes `+1.6 · a strong push toward` and the panel `+1.6 — a strong push
288	  toward`; that difference is the plan's.

296	  component and cannot disagree. Three steps: **●●●** for `documented`, `historical`,
297	  `market_implied` · **●●** for `argued`, `user` · **●** for `asserted`, `simulated`. The mark is

313	### B5 — The path-product bar (INV-8)
314	
315	Select a claim and a bar appears beside the story sentence showing the **multiplied-out likelihood
316	of the steps of one route from the hypothesis to it**, and naming those steps. A chain of four
317	plausible steps is not a plausible chain, and the product is the number that says so.
318	
319	**Which route: the best-backed one** — over every route from the hypothesis to the claim, the one
320	whose *weakest arrow is strongest*. That is the same route the delta rail's ranking uses
321	([`diff-view.md`](diff-view.md)), so the product has one path-choosing rule in the whole product,
322	used twice. On Hormuz, M1 is reached by `H → B → M1` and by `H → C → B → M1`; every arrow on both is
323	`argued`, so their weakest arrows tie, and the tie goes to **the shorter** *(proposed here — the
324	rule for ties belongs in `spec/multiverse/diff.md`, which stack 03a writes)*. The bar shows
325	`H → B → M1`:
326	
327	```
328	H → B → M1            the strait reopens, Brent settles below $68, and the
329	                      Polymarket contract resolves YES
330	path likelihood       —  no engine yet
331	```
332	
333	* **The product arrives on the world. This stack renders it and never multiplies anything itself.**
334	  If it is absent the bar says so with its reason; it does not fall back to computing.
335	* **Three things the bar can say, and they are not the same thing.** The number, when there is one.
336	  **"no path shown"** — nothing is selected, or no route was asked for; the absent-number case.
337	  **"no path from the hypothesis reaches this claim any more"** — a fact about the map after your
338	  edits, and the place that fact now lives: it stopped being a diff state on the tile (Kent,
339	  2026-09-17) because it is a property of the *route*, not of the claim. The bar never disappears; a
340	  missing bar looks like a bar nobody needed.
341	* **The honest wart, stated beside the number rather than hidden:** the factors are each read on
342	  their **own resolve-by day** — H by Nov 1, B by Oct 15, M1 by Oct 31 — so the product multiplies
343	  numbers read on three different days, and not even in order. It is still the most honest single number available for a chain,
344	  and **it is not a joint probability**. The panel says that in those words (decision record
345	  0014 §E).

359	### B7 — This generation: the working
360	
361	*(Decided 2026-09-17, stack 04a; this closes open question 2 below. **Amended 2026-09-21**: the
362	receipt's ten readings left this section — see below.)*
363	
364	NFR-6 says every generation records the model, the tokens, the cache reads, the searches and the
365	dollars, and shows them in the Inspector's transcript view. Nothing generated in the stack that wrote
366	this chapter, so nothing was specified and nothing was drawn. A generation now exists, and this is
367	where its **working** is read: what it was run against, and every proposal it made, in order.
368	
369	**What it cost is not here, and this section points at where it is** *(2026-09-21)*. The ten
370	readings were drawn twice — on the strip beside the map and again here — one above the other in a
371	320-pixel column. Two copies of one cost read, to somebody scrolling past, as two costs, and this was
372	the copy no number on screen could be traced to: the strip is what the `receipt` event fills in. So
373	the strip keeps them, in one place, and this section carries one sentence saying so.
374	
375	**The generation is the panel's third subject.** Until now the panel opened on a claim or an arrow.
376	It also opens on the run that produced them — `{ kind: "generation", id }`, where `id` is the
377	identifier the engine minted and sent on `generation_started`. It is not a claim and not an arrow, so
378	it gets its own section rather than being squeezed into one:
379	
380	```
381	THIS GENERATION
382	  the run that built this map
383	
384	WHAT IT WAS RUN AGAINST
385	  seed                 <GenerationStarted.seed, as its digits>
386	  prompt fingerprint   <Receipt.prompt_hash, whole>
387	
388	  The prompt fingerprint says which wording of our instructions produced this run:
389	  two runs with the same fingerprint were asked the same way, and two with different
390	  ones were not, however alike their maps look. It is printed whole because half a
391	  fingerprint cannot be compared with anything.
392	
393	  What this run cost is on the strip beside the map, in ten readings, every one of
394	  them a field the engine sent.
395	
396	EVERY PROPOSAL, IN ORDER
397	  0   accepted   The Strait of Hormuz is open to unrestricted commercial transit for
398	                 14 consecutive days
399	  …
400	  6   refused    "cheaper crude reduces the incentive to close the strait"
401	                 These claims form a loop with no delay in it: … Mark the arrow where a
402	                 market feeds back on the world as reflexive and give it a delay, or
403	                 remove one arrow.
404	  7   accepted   The energy fund XLE underperforms the S&P 500 fund SPY by more than
405	                 3% over 20 trading days
406	  —   stopped    Nothing further to add on "Lloyd's war-risk insurance premium for Gulf
407	                 transits falls below 0.4%"
408	  —   stopped    Nothing further to add on "Brent crude settles below $68 for five
409	                 sessions"
410	```
411	
412	*(The `→ H` and `→ M2` this sketch used to carry are gone, corrected 2026-09-21: the code has never
413	drawn them and must not. On a generated map an identifier is twenty-six characters of the engine's
414	own bookkeeping, and a reader learns nothing from one — INV-workbench.55. An accepted line names the
415	claim it became by quoting the claim.)*
416	
417	**Three kinds of line, not two.** A proposal was accepted, a proposal was refused, or the model
418	answered *Stop* on a line and it closed with nothing added. The third is the one a reader would
419	otherwise never see: it makes no event on the stream, because nothing about the map changed, and the
420	transcript is the only place it is recorded. **A stopped line carries no `at`** — `at` counts what was
421	proposed, and a stop proposed nothing — so the positions in this list have gaps in them, and the gaps
422	are the stops. Printing them as a dash rather than renumbering is what keeps `at` meaning the same
423	thing here as it does on the stream and in the refusal strip.
424	
425	Five rules, and four of them are rules this panel already obeys. *(Two of them have moved with the
426	readings: what follows about the cost and the mode is now the strip's, in
427	[`streaming-growth.md`](streaming-growth.md) B6, and is kept here because it is still what a reader
428	of this chapter needs to know about a number they clicked through from.)*
429	
430	* **Every number is a field, and the panel adds nothing up.** It does not total the two token counts,
431	  does not work a cost out of a token count and a price, and does not time anything. Searches have
432	  their own row because they are billed apart from tokens, so a reader checking `cost` against the
433	  token counts alone would find it wrong. INV-workbench.54 already forbids the arithmetic for
434	  likelihoods; the same rule covers a cost.
435	* **Every line of the transcript is in the engine's own words.** An accepted line names the claim it
436	  became; a refused line quotes what the model wrote and then carries the validator's own sentence,
437	  one per rule broken, with nothing added; a stopped line carries the model's own one-sentence reason.
438	  The panel composes no sentence about any of the three, and a refused claim is quoted rather than
439	  given an identifier or a tile.
440	* **The mode is read first.** On the strip, in a replay, the row says `replay` and names the day the
441	  recording was made — and **nothing else** *(amended 2026-09-21)*: it also carried the first eight
442	  characters of the prompt's fingerprint, which is a reading the browser derived on a strip whose
443	  whole promise is that none of them is, and is in any case a fingerprint nobody can check against
444	  anything. The fingerprint is printed whole here, with the sentence saying what it is for. The cost
445	  reads what the rebuilt receipt carries — zero, because the recording was played and nothing was
446	  called. That zero is a computed zero, printed rather than hidden (record 0012).
447	* **Before the receipt arrives, no cost is drawn anywhere.** No running estimate, no partial total,
448	  no ticking cost. A cost nobody has totalled is a number nobody computed, which is the same rule as
449	  the reserved band slot's in B3. **This section, though, is drawn from the moment there is a
450	  generation** *(corrected 2026-09-21: this said the section is not drawn, and stood above a section
451	  the code drew anyway, with *no engine yet* in it)*. It holds the working, not the cost, and the
452	  working is the thing a reader opens the panel for while a run is still going. Each slot that has
453	  not arrived reads an em dash. A section that appeared only once everything had landed would be a
454	  panel that is empty exactly while a reader is most likely to open it.
455	* **The two-significant-figures rule is about likelihoods.** A token count, a call count, a duration
456	  and a dollar figure are counts and measurements: they are printed whole, in `--font-mono` with
457	  fixed-width digits, and they carry no range because nothing sampled them. INV-workbench.36 is
458	  phrased over beliefs for exactly this reason.
459	
460	**Where it is read from, and how long it lasts.** `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript`, and
461	the server holds it in memory for the life of the process. There is no storage in this stack, so a
462	transcript does not outlive the server — FR-13's *"transcripts are stored with the graph"* arrives
463	with the SQLite file in stack 05 (FR-31). Until then, a transcript the process no longer has renders
464	as an absence with that reason, in the words of the route's own answer, rather than as an empty
465	section a reader would read as a transcript with nothing in it.
466	
467	**How you get here.** Selecting a row on the refusal strip opens the panel at that transcript line.
468	Selecting the receipt strip opens it at the top. Both strips, and the shape of the stream behind
469	them, are [`streaming-growth.md`](streaming-growth.md)'s; this chapter owns only what the panel does
470	with them, and INV-workbench.72 there pins the receipt's own fields.

539	**INV-workbench.58 — every claim can be scored.** For every claim the panel opens, the resolution
540	criteria, the adjudicating source and the resolve-by date all render, none optional and none
541	abbreviated (INV-1). *Test:* inspector › `test_always_renders_all_three_resolution_fields`.
542	
543	**INV-workbench.59 — a source says when it was fetched, or says nobody did.** For every source on an
544	arrow, the panel renders the day our retrieval step fetched it, or the reason there is no day. A
545	source with no retrieval day is never rendered as though it had one. *Test:* inspector ›
546	`test_renders_a_fetch_day_or_its_reason`.
547	
548	---
549	
550	## ANTI-PATTERNS
551	
552	1. **Do not open a dialog for anything — not evidence, not a confirmation, not an error.** *Because*
553	   a modal steals the map you were reading, and the map is what makes the detail mean anything; it
554	   is also a named veto condition. **Instead:** one persistent panel, and confirmations as undoable
555	   toasts.
556	
557	2. **Do not compute the decomposition in the browser from the pushes on the arrows.** *Because* the
558	   pieces are all there and the temptation is real — prior, three pushes, a result — and the moment
559	   the canvas does its own arithmetic there are two engines that disagree about half a point, with
560	   nobody able to say which is right. **Instead:** print the prior, the pushes and the result as
561	   the fields they each are, and an absence with its reason wherever one of them is not there.
562	
563	3. **Do not put a plausible sentence in the reserved band slot to show what it will look like, and
564	   do not print the uncalibrated label over a number nothing computed.** *Because* a sentence naming
565	   a percentage nobody computed is a number nobody computed wearing words, and "uncalibrated" over a
566	   stated range claims an arithmetic that never ran. **Instead:** the stated sentence and no slot
567	   until `versions` says otherwise; a comment naming `range_shares`; stack 06 fills it.
568	
569	4. **Do not average, blend or reconcile the three owners** — stated as an anti-pattern in
570	   [`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md), which owns the belief chip. Here it means three
571	   rows, three owners, and a difference computed outside and labelled one.
572	
573	5. **Do not let the Inspector spell provenance one way while the wire draws it another.** *Because*
574	   two renderings of one field drift within a week, and then the canvas and the panel tell a reader
575	   two different things about the same arrow. **Instead:** one `OriginMark`, used by both, with the
576	   word only ever here.
577	
578	6. **Do not print the path product as a joint probability.** *Because* its factors are read on
579	   different days and it is not the chance of the whole chain happening together; claiming that
580	   would be a fabrication in the place the honesty bar exists to prevent one. **Instead:** the
581	   number, the story beside it, and the wart said out loud.
582	
583	7. **Do not truncate the claim's wording here.** *Because* the tile already ellipsizes to three
584	   lines and this is where the full text lives; a claim you cannot read in full cannot be argued
585	   with. **Instead:** the whole sentence, wrapping as far as it needs.
586	
587	---
588	
589	## Open questions
590	
591	*Raised 2026-09-17. Four questions this chapter opened were settled by Kent the same day and now
592	read as statements in the body: which words a push reads back as (five bands, B4), which route the
593	path bar shows (B5), which sentence sits under the model row (B1), and where the "no market" reason
594	comes from (B1).*
595	
596	1. **Where does "falsified if" come from?** FR-10 lists it among the panel's contents and no field on
597	   a claim carries it: the resolution criteria read backwards, or a genuinely missing field on
598	   `Proposition`. **Owner:** `spec/graph/proposition.md`.
599	
600	2. **Where do generation cost and the transcript live?**
601	   **Decided 2026-09-17 (stack 04a): in the panel's own section, on a third subject.** The panel
602	   opens on a generation as well as on a claim and an arrow; the section prints the `receipt`
603	   event's fields one by one and the transcript beneath them, and is read from
604	   `GET /api/generate/{generation_id}/transcript`, which lives in memory for the life of the process
605	   until stack 05's file. In B7, and pinned by INV-workbench.54 here and INV-workbench.72 in
606	   [`streaming-growth.md`](streaming-growth.md).
607	
608	3. **May the panel show an arrow's pushes before the engine, without the result line?**
609	   **Decided 2026-09-17 (stack 04a), restated 2026-09-20 on building it: the question does not
610	   arise.** Every line of the block is always drawn, and a line with no number says its absence and
611	   why — so the result line reads *"no engine yet"* rather than being left off, and there is no
612	   half block to build. In B2.
613	
614	4. **"no reference class recorded for this claim"** *(proposed here)* is wording the interface wrote
615	   rather than a field it read, exactly as the "no market" sentences were before Kent settled them.
616	   If it is kept, it belongs beside them in [`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md). **Owner:**
617	   `vocabulary.md`.
618
